transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, thanks. Um, so what finally made me actually make an appointment is that I just keep turning in these applications, or like, my research notes, and they have these small but really embarrassing mistakes in them. Like, I'll completely mislabel an artwork date. 

Which reminds me, I was doing this deep dive on post-impressionism the other day, and it's crazy how Van Gogh's later stuff completely shifted in color palette after he moved to Arles. I actually really want to visit the south of France someday. My roommate went last summer and said the food was just incredible, especially this one little cafe they found near the beach... 

Wait, sorry, what was I saying? Right, the mistakes. Yeah, so I'll get the dates wrong on the art, or I'll just skip an entire question on an application form. And the weirdest part is that I honestly thought I had checked them. Like, I really sit there and proofread it, but then the errors are still just sitting there staring at me later.
Do you think you were paying attention when you were proofreading the applications and research notes?

I mean, I really thought I was! Like, I'll sit down at my desk—oh, I just got this new desk lamp, by the way. It's one of those daylight simulation ones because my room gets zero natural light. It's supposed to help with mood and focus, which I definitely need. I think it's working a little? But anyway, yeah, I'll sit there under the lamp, and I'll read through everything. I'll look right at the dates on the artwork, or the questions on the form, and it feels like I'm paying attention. But then later, someone points out the mistake, or I look again, and it's like my brain just completely glossed over it the first time. I really thought I had checked them, you know? It's just so frustrating.
Do you often find your mind wandering away from what you're doing at other times, not just when proofreading?

Yeah, all the time. Like, if I'm trying to read or write at my desk... oh, wait, I didn't even mention, I live right by this really busy intersection now. It's so loud. They're doing construction on the corner, and they've been doing it for like three months. I don't even know what they're building, but they start at like 7 AM. 

But anyway, yeah, I'll be trying to work, and then a siren will go by outside, or I'll hear people talking out in the hallway of my apartment building. My neighbors are actually pretty cool, they have this adorable corgi that always tries to sneak into my apartment when I open the door. He's so cute. 

But yeah, if I hear a noise, or even if I just have a random thought pop into my head—like, I'll suddenly get an idea for how to curate an exhibit on, I don't know, brutalist architecture or something—I'll just completely lose track of what I was doing. And then I'll realize like twenty minutes later that I haven't written a single word. It's like my brain just takes a detour and forgets to come back.
Do you often feel anxious or on edge?

Anxious? Um, no, not really. I don't think I feel on edge. Actually, my mom is the one who gets super anxious about everything. She called me yesterday completely freaking out because she watched this documentary about deep-sea creatures. Have you ever looked into that? Like the anglerfish, with the little glowing light on their heads? It's honestly wild how they survive down there with zero sunlight and all that water pressure. I ended up going down this massive internet rabbit hole watching videos about the Mariana Trench instead of doing my laundry. It's crazy to think we know more about the surface of Mars than our own oceans, you know? Like, they keep sending rovers up there, and... wait, sorry. What was the question? Oh, right, if I feel on edge. Yeah, no, I'm usually pretty chill.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety?

Restless? Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I fidget that much. I guess sometimes I tap my foot if I'm listening to music, but that's just keeping the beat, right? Oh man, I actually just got these new noise-canceling headphones, and they are incredible. Like, game-changers. I can finally listen to my playlists without hearing that construction outside. I've been really into this one indie band lately, they use a lot of synth and weird time signatures. It's super cool. I actually tried to learn how to play the synthesizer a few years ago. I bought this little portable one online, but I couldn't figure out how to program it. It had all these tiny knobs and buttons, and the manual was translated really badly, so it made zero sense. I think it's still sitting in the back of my closet somewhere. I should probably sell it. Do you think there's a big market for used, slightly confusing synthesizers? Anyway, yeah, I don't really feel fidgety. I mostly just sit there.
Do you often have trouble finishing things you start?

Trouble finishing things? Um... I guess maybe sometimes? But not really anything major. Like, I'll start a book and maybe not finish it, but that's just because I get bored. I actually started reading this sci-fi novel last week about terraforming Mars. It was super interesting at first, like all the science behind how they'd have to melt the ice caps to create an atmosphere. It reminded me of this documentary I saw about how they grow plants on the International Space Station. Did you know they grew radishes up there? Or maybe it was lettuce. I can't remember. But imagine being an astronaut and just eating space lettuce. I always wanted to go to space camp when I was a kid, but my parents sent me to this weird nature camp instead where we just learned how to tie knots. I still know how to tie a bowline, actually. It's surprisingly useful when you're moving furniture. I helped my buddy move his couch last month and we had to tie it to the roof of his car. We drove like ten miles an hour the whole way because we were terrified it was gonna fly off. But anyway, no, I don't think I have a huge problem finishing things. I just move on if I'm not into it.
Do you have trouble keeping your attention on a single task for a long period of time?

Attention on a single task? Um, no, not really. I mean, if I'm doing something I actually care about, I can sit there for hours. Like, I just got this new open-world RPG, and the map is absolutely massive. You can just walk in any direction and find, like, hidden caves or weird NPCs giving out quests. The voice acting is actually pretty good, too, which is rare. Usually, in those games, the characters sound like they're reading off a teleprompter, you know? It reminds me of this public speaking class I had to take for my bachelor's. We had to do a ten-minute presentation on a historical figure, and this one guy literally just read the entire Wikipedia page for Alexander the Great off his phone. The professor was so mad. He was this really intense guy who always wore bow ties. I kind of respect the bow tie look, honestly. It takes confidence. I bought one for a wedding once, but I could not figure out how to tie it, so I just used a clip-on. Nobody could tell the difference anyway. The food at that wedding was amazing, though. They had a mashed potato bar. Have you ever seen one of those? You just get a martini glass full of potatoes and put whatever you want on it. It's genius. But, uh... wait. Did you ask about my attention span? Yeah, no, I'm pretty good at focusing, I think.
Do you have trouble organizing your time or tasks?

Organizing my time? Uh, I mean, I guess it's not great. Like, my apartment is basically just a bunch of half-started projects everywhere right now. I've got rent papers mixed up with these notes I took at an art gallery, and my laptop is even worse. My desktop is just covered in, like, random article PDFs and fifty different to-do lists, and I have a really hard time figuring out what actually needs to happen first. Oh, speaking of art galleries, I went to this really weird modern art exhibit downtown last week. It was all, like, sculptures made out of recycled electronics. There was this huge one that was just old flip phones glued together to look like a giant wave. It was actually kind of sad, thinking about all those old phones. Remember the Motorola Razr? Man, I wanted one of those so badly when I was in middle school. The silver one. Everybody had one, and they would do that dramatic snap when they hung up on someone. You can't really dramatically hang up on a smartphone. You just kind of aggressively tap the screen, which isn't the same. I actually tried to buy a refurbished Razr on eBay a couple of months ago just for the nostalgia, but the guy never shipped it. I had to go through this whole dispute process with PayPal. Have you ever had to do that? It takes forever. They make you wait like two weeks before they even look at it. But anyway, yeah, organizing stuff is kind of tough for me. I just never know where to start with all the lists and papers.
Do you have trouble managing your emotions when you make those embarrassing mistakes on applications or research notes?

Managing my emotions? Um, not really, no. I mean, I don't really get super upset or anything. It's more just like an "oops" moment, you know? Like, I'll realize I messed up a date on a form or skipped a line in my notes, and I just fix it if I can. It's not a big deal. Speaking of notes, I was actually looking through some old notebooks from my freshman year the other day. I was trying to find this recipe for banana bread that my roommate wrote down for me. He was from Hawaii, and he swore his family's recipe was the best in the world. He used, like, way more butter than you'd think is legal. We used to make it in our dorm kitchen at like 2 AM. That kitchen was always a disaster, though. Someone always left their dishes in the sink for days. One time, someone left a whole pot of spaghetti in there, and it literally started growing mold. It was disgusting. We had to call the RA to come deal with it because nobody wanted to touch it. Our RA was this really chill guy who played ultimate frisbee. He actually tried to get me to join the team, but I'm terrible at throwing a frisbee. It always just goes straight into the ground or off to the side. Have you ever played ultimate frisbee? It's way more running than you'd expect. But, uh, yeah, no, I don't really get emotional about mistakes. I just kind of brush it off.
Do you have trouble motivating yourself to start tasks or activities?

Motivating myself? Yeah, definitely. If I know something is going to take real concentration, like, say I have to draft a curatorial proposal or read some really dense art theory chapter for my degree, I just... I can't start it. I'll put it off by doing a million smaller errands instead. Like, I'll suddenly decide I need to reorganize my bookshelf by color, which is a terrible system by the way because you can never find the book you actually need. I tried it once and spent an hour looking for my copy of *The Great Gatsby* because I forgot the spine was actually dark blue and not black. We had to read that in high school, and my teacher, Mr. Harrison, was obsessed with the green light. He talked about it for like three weeks straight. He had this weird habit of pacing back and forth across the front of the room while he talked, and his shoes squeaked on the linoleum. It was so distracting. I actually hate linoleum floors. They just feel so institutional, you know? Like a hospital or a cafeteria. Oh man, the cafeteria in my middle school served these square pizzas on Fridays. They were so greasy, but everyone loved them. You had to get in line early or they'd run out and you'd be stuck with the mystery meatloaf. I always tried to trade my apple slices for an extra slice of pizza. Sometimes it worked if the other kid was really into fruit. But anyway, yeah, I'll just do all these random little things until it's suddenly the night before the big project is due, and then I'm panicking. So starting the hard stuff is definitely a problem.
Do you find that you lose interest in tasks before you finish them?

Lose interest halfway through? Um, no, not really. I don't really have that problem. If I actually manage to start something, I'll usually stick with it until it's done. Like, I was doing this huge puzzle the other day... it was a thousand pieces of Starry Night. Van Gogh, you know? Though honestly, I've always preferred post-impressionism over just straight impressionism. Like Seurat is so fascinating with the pointillism. Can you imagine having the patience to paint an entire canvas using only tiny little dots? I went to Chicago once and saw *A Sunday on La Grande Jatte* in person at the Art Institute. Have you ever been there? It's massive. The painting, I mean, but the museum too. We took the Amtrak down there for a weekend trip, and the dining car was out of order, so we had to survive on these awful vending machine pretzels for like six hours. They were so dry, it was like eating actual sand. I ended up buying a ridiculously overpriced ginger ale just to wash them down. I don't even really like ginger ale, honestly. It always makes me think of being sick when I was a kid. My mom would always give me room-temperature ginger ale and saltines when I had the stomach flu, and we'd just sit on the couch and watch The Price is Right. Bob Barker, man, what a legend. The new guy just isn't the same, the energy is totally different. But, uh, what was I saying? Oh, right, finishing things. Yeah, I don't really lose interest once I'm actually going. I finished that whole puzzle in like two days.
Do you have intense mood swings?

Intense mood swings? No, I don't think so. I mean, my mood stays pretty level most of the time. I'm not really one of those people who goes from super happy to really angry out of nowhere. I had a roommate like that once, though, back in my sophomore year. His name was Greg, and he would just snap over the smallest things. Like, one time I used his special non-stick pan to make a grilled cheese, and he completely lost his mind because I used a metal spatula. Which, okay, I know you're not supposed to do that, but he acted like I had keyed his car or something. He had this really nice car, actually. It was an old vintage Mustang, cherry red. He spent all his free time working on it in the campus parking lot. I don't know anything about cars, honestly. I've always just driven whatever cheap sedan I could afford. Right now I have this beat-up Honda Civic that makes a weird rattling noise whenever I go over 60 miles an hour. I took it to a mechanic, and he told me it was some issue with the heat shield, but he wanted like three hundred bucks to fix it, and I just couldn't afford that on a student budget. You know how expensive textbooks are? It's a complete scam. I had to pay two hundred dollars for an art history book that we literally only used for two chapters. I tried to sell it back at the end of the semester, and the bookstore offered me twelve dollars. Twelve! It's ridiculous. I ended up just keeping it to use as a monitor stand for my laptop. It works pretty well for that, actually. But, um, yeah, mood swings. No, I don't really have those. I'm pretty steady.
Do you often struggle with feeling motivated to do things you know you need to do?

Wait, didn't we just talk about this? Like, motivating myself to start things? I feel like we just covered that. Unless you mean... well, no, I think I already said how I put things off by organizing my bookshelf or whatever. Did I mention the linoleum floors? I definitely mentioned Mr. Harrison. He was the one who paced. Seriously, squeak, squeak, squeak, all period long. It's a wonder any of us passed that class. I think half the class was just asleep anyway because it was right after lunch. Lunch was always such a chaotic time in high school. You had to find a table with your friends before the seniors took all the good spots by the windows. We always got stuck near the trash cans. It smelled like old ketchup and bleach. I hate the smell of bleach. It reminds me of the public pool I used to go to when I was a kid. I almost drowned there once, actually. Well, not drowned, but I swallowed a lot of water and choked for a while. The lifeguard had to blow his whistle and everything. It was super embarrassing. My mom made me take private swimming lessons after that. The instructor was this guy named Chad who wore zinc on his nose like it was the 1980s. He was really intense about proper kicking technique. But, uh... yeah, I'm pretty sure I already answered the motivation thing. Unless I'm confused?
Do you find it hard to focus on a single task for a long time, like more than a few hours?

Focus on one thing for a few hours? Um, no, not really. I mean, I don't think I have a hard time with that. If I'm doing something, I can usually just do it. Like playing video games. I can sit there and play for hours. I got really into this one game last month, Stardew Valley. Have you played it? It's like a farming simulator, but there's so much more to it. You can mine, and fish, and talk to the townspeople. I spent an entire weekend just trying to catch this one legendary fish. The fishing mechanic is actually kind of tricky, you have to keep the fish inside this little green bar that bounces up and down. I ended up looking up a guide online because I kept losing it. The guy in the video had this crazy setup with all these monitors and neon lights in his room. I don't really get the whole RGB lighting trend, honestly. It seems like it would just hurt your eyes after a while. My eyes get dry pretty easily anyway. I have to use those lubricating drops, the ones in the little single-use vials. My eye doctor told me I don't blink enough when I look at screens. He had all these weird posters in his waiting room about, like, the anatomy of the eyeball. It was kind of gross, actually, seeing all the veins and stuff. But, um... what was the question? Oh, focusing for a long time. Yeah, I don't really think that's an issue for me. I can focus just fine if I'm doing something.
Do you have trouble calming down when you get upset or frustrated?

Trouble calming down? I don't... I don't think so. I mean, if I get frustrated, I usually just get over it pretty quick. I'm not the type to hold onto things. My sister, though, she holds a grudge like nobody's business. One time when we were kids, I accidentally broke one of her porcelain horses. She had this whole collection of them lined up on a shelf in her room. They were super fragile, and I was throwing a tennis ball against the wall, which my mom always told me not to do inside, but it was raining outside. It rained for like three days straight that week. Our basement actually flooded a little bit, and my dad had to rent this massive wet vac from Home Depot. The guy at the rental counter was really rude to him, I remember my dad complaining about it for the entire drive home. He said the guy acted like renting out equipment was some huge favor he was doing us. Anyway, the wet vac was so loud, it sounded like a jet engine taking off in the house. Our dog hated it. He hid under the couch the whole time it was running. He was a Golden Retriever mix, super sweet but afraid of loud noises. Thunderstorms, fireworks, the vacuum cleaner... he'd just cower and shake. We tried one of those thunder shirts for him, but it didn't really seem to help much. He looked ridiculous in it, too, like a little sausage casing. But, um... yeah, getting upset. I don't really have a hard time calming down. I just kind of move on.
Do you find that you can maintain your focus on a task for as long as you need to, or do you find your attention drifting away before you've completed it?

Maintain focus... um, no, my attention definitely drifts. Like, if I'm sitting at my desk trying to read or write something, I get pulled away super easily. If there's a siren outside, or if I hear someone talking in the hallway... which happens all the time, honestly, because the acoustics in my building are just terrible. The floors are hardwood, so every single footstep echoes. My upstairs neighbor walks like he's wearing cinderblocks on his feet. I think he works night shifts or something because he's always stomping around at 3 AM. I tried wearing those little foam earplugs, but they always fall out while I'm sleeping. Then I end up finding them tangled in the sheets days later, which is kind of gross. I actually read this article about how you're supposed to roll them up really tight before you put them in so they expand in your ear, but it never works for me. They just pop right back out. 

But, uh, anyway, where was I? Oh, right, drifting away. Yeah, even if it's completely quiet, just a random thought will pop into my head. Like I'll get this random thought about an exhibit idea, and my brain just completely runs with it. And then, I don't know, twenty minutes will go by before I even notice that I haven't been reading at all. So, yeah, I definitely don't just stay on task until it's done.
Do you find that your difficulties with attention and completing tasks are affecting your daily life and relationships?

Affecting my life? Yeah, I guess it is. Because of all this, I’ve submitted work late, and I actually missed a couple of application deadlines recently. One was for this fellowship, and the application portal was just terribly designed. It kept logging me out every five minutes. Plus it had this tiny file size limit for PDFs, so I had to find a site to compress my files, and the site was covered in ads. I ended up clicking on one for a mattress company because I’ve been waking up with a really sore lower back lately. My mattress is just a cheap memory foam one I got off Amazon, and I think it’s already sagging in the middle. I read you're supposed to rotate them every six months, but it's so heavy, and my room is basically a closet. I can barely fit my desk in there, let alone flip a queen-size mattress around. The desk chair I have is awful too, one of the wheels is broken so it just scrapes against the floor... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, my attention affecting things. Right. Yeah, so I missed those deadlines. And my mentor actually sat me down recently and told me my follow-through is starting to hurt opportunities I should be ready for. Which was pretty rough to hear, honestly.
Do you think your difficulties with attention and completing tasks are causing you significant distress or problems in your daily life?

Distress? Yeah, I mean, it's definitely causing problems. Like I was just saying, I've been turning things in late, and missing those application deadlines really stung. The fellowship one especially, because I spent so much time just trying to get the formatting right on my resume. I used this template I found online, but it had these weird column breaks that kept messing up the text alignment. I spent like three hours trying to fix it, and then I realized the font I was using wasn't even standard. It was some custom font I downloaded for a typography project last semester. That project was a nightmare, by the way. We had to design a full alphabet based on a specific architectural style, and I chose Art Deco. I love the look of it, all those geometric shapes and sleek lines. Have you ever seen the Chrysler Building in New York? It's gorgeous, especially when the sun hits the spire. I went there on a school trip in high school, and we took this double-decker bus tour. The tour guide had the most monotone voice, though. Half the bus fell asleep by the time we got to Central Park. 

But, um... wait, what was the question? Oh, right, distress and problems. Yeah, it's a problem. Missing those deadlines is bad, and having my mentor tell me my lack of follow-through is hurting my chances for opportunities... that really stressed me out. It's just frustrating knowing I should be ready for these things, but I keep getting in my own way.
Do you think your difficulties with attention and completing tasks are more related to being easily distracted or having trouble sustaining focus on the tasks themselves?

More related to being easily distracted or trouble sustaining focus? I mean, I guess it's both? Or maybe I don't really know the difference. Like, I definitely get distracted by things around me, but even if there's nothing going on, my brain just won't stay on the thing I'm supposed to be doing. It's like trying to hold onto water, you know? It just slips through your fingers. Speaking of water, I really need to buy a new Brita filter. The light on my pitcher has been blinking red for like three weeks, and the water is starting to taste kind of metallic. I think the pipes in my building are super old. The super told me once that the building was constructed in the 1920s, which is cool historically, but the plumbing is a disaster. The water pressure in the shower is basically a trickle. I bought one of those fancy showerheads that's supposed to increase pressure, but I couldn't get the old one off. It's like rusted onto the pipe. I tried using WD-40, but it just made my whole bathroom smell like a mechanic's garage. 

Wait, sorry. Distracted or sustaining focus. Um, I don't really know which one it is more of. I just know that I can't seem to stay on track with what I'm doing, whether it's because of something else catching my attention or just my own thoughts wandering off.
Do you think your difficulties with attention and completing tasks are causing you more problems in your daily life than any other issues you might be experiencing?

More problems than anything else? I mean, I'm not really sure how to weigh them against each other. It's definitely the main thing that's messing up my schoolwork right now. But is it the *biggest* problem? I don't know. I guess I haven't really thought about it like a competition. Speaking of competitions, my roommate just entered this massive Super Smash Bros tournament over the weekend. He was practicing for weeks, just constantly playing. The clicking of his controller was driving me insane. He plays Fox, and apparently, you have to do these really fast inputs to be good. He ended up getting knocked out in the second round, though. He was so mad he actually threw his controller at the couch. It bounced off a cushion and knocked over my favorite coffee mug—the one I got from that pottery class I took last summer. It was supposed to be a bowl, but the sides collapsed while it was on the wheel, so I just added a handle and called it a mug. The glaze on it was this really cool speckled blue... 

Sorry, I'm doing it again. Um, whether it's my biggest problem... I honestly couldn't tell you for sure. It's definitely up there, but I don't know if it's the absolute worst thing.

target_item.name: Detail_Inattention_Errors

patient.answer: I mean, I really thought I was! Like, I'll sit down at my desk—oh, I just got this new desk lamp, by the way. It's one of those daylight simulation ones because my room gets zero natural light. It's supposed to help with mood and focus, which I definitely need. I think it's working a little? But anyway, yeah, I'll sit there under the lamp, and I'll read through everything. I'll look right at the dates on the artwork, or the questions on the form, and it feels like I'm paying attention. But then later, someone points out the mistake, or I look again, and it's like my brain just completely glossed over it the first time. I really thought I had checked them, you know? It's just so frustrating.

doctor.intent: determine if the patient experiences mind wandering or distractibility frequently in daily life

target_item.name: Distractibility
target_item.manifestation: When I’m trying to read or write at my desk, a siren outside, someone talking in the hallway, or even a random thought about an exhibit idea can pull me away for twenty minutes before I notice.

patient.answer:
Yeah, all the time. Like, if I'm trying to read or write at my desk... oh, wait, I didn't even mention, I live right by this really busy intersection now. It's so loud. They're doing construction on the corner, and they've been doing it for like three months. I don't even know what they're building, but they start at like 7 AM. 

But anyway, yeah, I'll be trying to work, and then a siren will go by outside, or I'll hear people talking out in the hallway of my apartment building. My neighbors are actually pretty cool, they have this adorable corgi that always tries to sneak into my apartment when I open the door. He's so cute. 

But yeah, if I hear a noise, or even if I just have a random thought pop into my head—like, I'll suddenly get an idea for how to curate an exhibit on, I don't know, brutalist architecture or something—I'll just completely lose track of what I was doing. And then I'll realize like twenty minutes later that I haven't written a single word. It's like my brain just takes a detour and forgets to come back.
